title: Audit event (C8)
description: One JSON object per line on a dedicated logger/appender shipped to the SIEM. Never contains argument values, tool results, secrets, confirmation codes, TOTP codes, authenticator seeds or otpauth URIs; additionalProperties is false so such fields cannot be added by accident. Target system of broker events is carried in 'server' (mcp-<system>). The serializer must escape control characters, U+2028 and U+2029 in every string value.

clientRequestId.description: X-Request-Id sent by the AI client, recorded by the gateway only (C3). Untrusted, so limited to a log-safe alphabet (CC-031); the gateway drops a value that does not match instead of rejecting the call.

backendUser.description: Account in the target system read by whoami (C4.1, CC-101), for connection_change: the only trace of which account a user connected (CC-117). Same length limit as username. Never a secret. Excluded characters: C0 and C1 control characters and DEL (also TAB, LF, CR), every Unicode format character (\p{Cf}: zero-width characters U+200B..U+200F, U+2060, U+FEFF, soft hyphen, bidirectional controls, Arabic letter mark U+061C, tag characters U+E0000..U+E007F), surrogates, U+2028, U+2029, noncharacters (U+FDD0..U+FDEF, U+FFFE, U+FFFF), the invisible fillers U+034F, U+115F, U+1160, U+3164, U+FFA0, U+2800 and the variation selectors U+FE00..U+FE0F. This is the set of the text hygiene of the README (CC-121), stricter for log fields since 3.0.2 (zero-width, direction marks and tag characters used to pass), so that the line-oriented SIEM format and log viewers cannot be misled (CC-031).

filter.description: Normalized query of the endpoint filter of the request (CC-170, CC-174), only when the request carried one; absent without a filter. Made of tokens that have the syntax of a system id or a qualified tool name and nothing else, so it is neither a secret nor personal data; the parser does not check that a token names a system or tool that exists, so the client chooses these tokens and the field is data from the client, not a list of the platform's systems (CC-186). Carried by the gateway on tool_call, policy_decision, confirmation and credential_resolve; never by authentication, by servers or by the broker (they do not receive the filter, correlation is by requestId).

action.description: Cedar action an administrator gave a tool of an adapter together with risk, on admin_change with reason definition_approved or risk_lowered_by_admin (CC-206); with risk it is the classification. Absent on every other event. An approval that carries both risk and action on a tool of an adapter is the classification of that tool.

id.description: Resource id as the system knows it (Jira key, GitLab path, index name, page id). Free-form because ids of the five systems use different alphabets (slashes, dots, spaces in some service desks). Excluded characters: C0 and C1 control characters and DEL (also TAB, LF, CR), every Unicode format character (\p{Cf}: zero-width characters U+200B..U+200F, U+2060, U+FEFF, soft hyphen, bidirectional controls, Arabic letter mark U+061C, tag characters U+E0000..U+E007F), surrogates, U+2028, U+2029, noncharacters (U+FDD0..U+FDEF, U+FFFE, U+FFFF), the invisible fillers U+034F, U+115F, U+1160, U+3164, U+FFA0, U+2800 and the variation selectors U+FE00..U+FE0F. This is the set of the text hygiene of the README (CC-121), stricter for log fields since 3.0.2 (zero-width, direction marks and tag characters used to pass), so that the line-oriented SIEM format and log viewers cannot be misled (CC-031). The length limit counts code points; producers should keep ids below 512 characters. Independently of this, the audit JSON serializer must escape every control character and U+2028/U+2029.

parent.description: Parent as <Namespace>::<Type>::<id>, e.g. Jira::Project::ABC (C8 example format). The id part has the same exclusions as resource.id: C0 and C1 control characters and DEL (also TAB, LF, CR), every Unicode format character (\p{Cf}: zero-width characters U+200B..U+200F, U+2060, U+FEFF, soft hyphen, bidirectional controls, Arabic letter mark U+061C, tag characters U+E0000..U+E007F), surrogates, U+2028, U+2029, noncharacters (U+FDD0..U+FDEF, U+FFFE, U+FFFF), the invisible fillers U+034F, U+115F, U+1160, U+3164, U+FFA0, U+2800 and the variation selectors U+FE00..U+FE0F. This is the set of the text hygiene of the README (CC-121), stricter for log fields since 3.0.2 (zero-width, direction marks and tag characters used to pass), so that the line-oriented SIEM format and log viewers cannot be misled (CC-031).

group.description: Group (C9) of a scope mapping entry, on admin_change events with reason scope_mapping_entry_removed (the entry of a deleted server's namespace), scope_mapping_entry_ignored (an entry that evaluation skipped because its scope no longer fits the declarations) or scope_mapping_changed. The scope id goes to resource: type is the resource type of the scope (the part before the slash, e.g. Jira::Project) and id the part after it, so the pair is the ResourceScope id <type>/<id>. Absent on every other event.

overrideId.description: Id of the emergency override on admin_change events with reason override_set, override_removed, override_invalid or override_rejected (7.0.0). Absent on every other event.

overrideTarget.description: Target of the override: gateway, all-servers or a serverId (same events as overrideId).

textSha256.description: sha256 of the Cedar text of the override after the change (override_set, override_invalid, override_rejected) or removed (override_removed); never the text itself.

textSha256Before.description: sha256 of the text before a replacement (override_set that replaces an override); absent for a create.

changedFields.description: Names of the fields a PATCH of a server changed, on admin_change with reason server_updated (credential, enabled); never their values.

reason.description: Machine-readable reason, snake case. Known values: policy_forbid, secret_stored_unverified, server_created, server_updated, server_deleted, server_connection_approved, server_connection_changed, scope_mapping_changed, scope_mapping_entry_removed, scope_mapping_entry_ignored, override_set, override_removed, override_invalid, override_rejected, policies_submitted, policies_approved, policies_changed, policy_data_invalid, system_created, system_updated, system_deleted, system_imported, service_account_key_set, service_account_key_deleted, connections_invalidated, not_admin, not_granted, tool_disabled, user_confirmed, user_confirmed_no_preview, confirmation_expired, attempts_exhausted, authenticator_not_registered, authenticator_disabled, superseded, pending_exists, cancelled_by_owner, credential_required, step_up_required, rate_limited, rate_limited_user, rate_limited_client, rate_limited_tool, exchange_denied, system_not_configured, subject_token_invalid, credential_type_mismatch, risk_lowered_by_admin, user_purged, unused_cleanup, definition_changed, tool_not_served, definition_submitted, wrong_purpose, filter_scope, invalid_filter, filter_mismatch, invalid_cursor, policy_unavailable, policy_error, kill_switch, kill_switch_set, kill_switch_cleared, hidden_characters, secret_missing, database_unavailable, refresh_token_lost, user_offboarding, secret_store_unavailable, token_refreshed, oauth_grant_revoked, connection_changed_during_refresh, provider_unavailable, connection_busy. credential_type_mismatch: on the gateway (event credential_resolve, outcome error, errorCode internal_error; credentialType is the type the broker returned) the broker returned a type that is not in the set of types the gateway configuration allows for the system; on a server (event policy_decision or tool_call) the type in X-MCP-Credential-Type, sent by the gateway with X-MCP-Credential, is not in the set of the server's accepted credential types, is missing or is not one of the four types, or the server has none configured, and the check comes before Cedar, the grant probe and the resolvers: decision deny, outcome error, errorCode internal_error, the client learns nothing more (CC-166). For rate limits (gateway, CC-156) a refused call or request is recorded as tool_call (a tools/call) or policy_decision (any other MCP request) with decision deny, outcome denied, errorCode rate_limited and reason rate_limited_user, rate_limited_client (the pair user and AI client) or rate_limited_tool (the pair user and tool); the client is not told which limit applied, the administrator is. The gateway may aggregate excess events as for CC-125. For event credential_resolve (broker, gateway): exchange_denied (the IdP refused the token exchange, CC-157, outcome denied; the gateway records it on the tool_call event of the call it had allowed, decision allow, outcome denied, errorCode access_denied, which is the normative shape for the activity row, CC-165) and system_not_configured (the system is not configured in the broker, CC-158, outcome error) and subject_token_invalid (the subject token of a token exchange has the wrong audience, has expired or belongs to another sub than the internal JWT, CC-157, outcome denied). For event connection_change (broker): user_purged (the connection was removed by the offboarding purge, CC-155) and unused_cleanup (the connection was removed because it had not been used for the configured number of days, 180 by default, CC-155). Both offboarding purges (broker and gateway) emit one admin_change with reason user_purged and outcome ok for every call, also when nothing was removed and for an unknown sub, so that a call of mcp-offboarding always leaves a trace (CC-155). For event confirmation (gateway, CC-094): confirmation_pending is the decision when the pending call is created, and the outcome is one of user_confirmed (code accepted), user_confirmed_no_preview (accepted although the owner did not open the portal preview), confirmation_expired, attempts_exhausted, authenticator_not_registered, authenticator_disabled, code_burned (the retry carried a code of a burned step: confirmation_failed outwards, no attempt spent, not a wrong code, CC-128), cancelled_by_owner (the owner cancelled the pending call in the portal, CC-128; decision deny, errorCode confirmation_cancelled, emitted when the cancel is accepted and again when the cancelled call is retried), pending_exists (a new DESTRUCTIVE call was refused because another one is pending and its preview was opened; errorCode confirmation_blocked, CC-127), superseded (the pending DESTRUCTIVE call was replaced by a newer one of the same user, CC-127; emitted for the older call when the newer is created, and again when the older call is retried); user_declined and preview_not_viewed are not emitted since 3.0.0 (there is no decline, and the preview is optional). For event authenticator (broker, portal, CC-094): authenticator_enrollment_started, authenticator_registered, authenticator_enrollment_failed, authenticator_removed, authenticator_reset_by_admin (outcome ok or denied; the target user is sub), authenticator_seed_missing (the seed of a registered authenticator is gone from the secret store: the registration is reset to none, outcome error, errorCode upstream_unavailable, CC-142), authenticator_disabled (the daily limit of 20 wrong codes in 24 hours switched the authenticator off, CC-126; outcome denied) and, for the check of a code with decision allow or deny, totp_verified, totp_invalid, totp_replayed, totp_locked, totp_disabled, totp_burned (a code of a burned step: replayed for the broker but not a failure and not counted, CC-128), totp_steps_burned (the current codes were invalidated because the owner cancelled a pending operation or a new DESTRUCTIVE operation followed a viewed one, CC-128; outcome ok), totp_not_registered (these carry tool and client from the internal JWT). For events of the broker (CC-196, CC-205), reasons that were not listed before 6.0.0 (the outcomes and error codes below are the ones the broker reports; ws-06 confirms them, and only database_unavailable, refresh_token_lost and secret_missing have vectors): database_unavailable (the database did not answer: the operation is refused with 503, outcome error, errorCode upstream_unavailable; also for the authenticator), secret_store_unavailable (the secret store did not answer, outcome error, errorCode upstream_unavailable), refresh_token_lost (the provider rotated the refresh token and the broker could not store the new one even after retries; the new tokens are revoked at the provider and the connection goes to error, not revoked; connection_change, outcome error), user_offboarding (a write was refused because a purge of the user is running or has just run, CC-155; outcome denied), token_refreshed (the access token was renewed, outcome ok), oauth_grant_revoked (the provider answered invalid_grant, the connection is revoked), connection_changed_during_refresh (the connection was replaced or deleted while it was being refreshed, so the refresh result was dropped), provider_unavailable (the provider did not answer, outcome error, errorCode upstream_unavailable), connection_busy (another refresh of the same connection holds the lock) and secret_missing (the secret of a connection is gone from the secret store: the broker sets the state of the connection to error so that the user connects again, connection_change, outcome error, CC-205). For event connection_change (broker) a failed revocation at the provider is recorded with reason provider_revoke_failed (the connection is deleted anyway, outcome error; CC-142). For tool_call and policy_decision: filter_scope (the tool exists and the user may call it, but the endpoint filter of the request leaves it out, decision deny, outcome denied, errorCode not_found_or_denied, CC-170, CC-178: checked before tool_disabled, upstream_unavailable and credential_required and before the confirmation gate), invalid_filter (the query of the request does not parse or exceeds a limit, policy_decision, decision deny, outcome error, without errorCode, CC-170), filter_mismatch (the route or the filter of the request differs from the ones bound to the MCP session, policy_decision, decision deny, outcome denied, CC-172, CC-184; a session of another user or an unknown one is a 404 without this reason), invalid_cursor (the cursor of tools/list is malformed, was changed or was issued to another user or for another filter, policy_decision, decision deny, outcome error, without errorCode, CC-181), These four refusals that a client can repeat at will (invalid_filter, filter_mismatch, invalid_cursor and a tools/call answered not_found_or_denied with not_granted or filter_scope) are written at most once per user and reason in an interval (10 s by default); the rest is only counted in mcp_audit_endpoint_suppressed_total{reason}, and the request is refused either way (CC-190, CC-191: the key of the interval is user, reason and target, and a summary event with suppressedCount follows each window), policy_unavailable (no policy bundle is loaded, so nothing can be decided and the request is refused), policy_error (the policy engine failed on this request) definition_changed (the definition the server presents differs from the approved one, so the tool is hidden and refused with errorCode tool_disabled, CC-133) upstream_unavailable (on tool_call or policy_decision: a store behind the check, such as the counter of the limits, the session store or the store of the emergency switches, did not answer and the request was refused, CC-167, CC-194, CC-199; also a request that the gateway shed because too many were in progress, CC-199, which the gateway may aggregate as in CC-125) and tool_not_served (the approved tool is missing from the tools the server serves, so it is hidden and refused with errorCode tool_disabled, CC-161). definition_changed and tool_not_served are recorded on every refused call (not once per read) and when a read finds the difference there is no separate event. A failed read of the server's tools/list is not evidence of either: the gateway keeps its last successful read, and a call that needs a fresh read that fails is refused as upstream_unavailable without a call to the server. kill_switch (tool_call, decision deny, outcome denied, errorCode tool_disabled: the tool or its server was switched off by an administrator, CC-194; tool_disabled alone is a definition waiting for approval or classification). At the tool level of the gateway policy_forbid is a refusal by a forbid rule (for example from the overrides bundle) answered not_found_or_denied, and not_granted means that no permit allowed the tool (CC-198); the activity row of the user for both stays denied_not_granted. On a server policy_forbid is a refusal by policy (a forbid rule or no permit) and not_granted a resource that could not be resolved or has no grant (CC-141). Event admin_change records the administrative changes of the gateway and of the broker. For the registry, with reasons definition_registered (the pipeline registered a manifest and the definition was approved by that call: a READ_ONLY tool, CC-133), definition_submitted (the registration left a new or changed UPDATE or DESTRUCTIVE tool pending approval, CC-133), definition_approved (an administrator approved a pending definition; sub is the administrator and definitionHash the approved hash) and risk_lowered_by_admin (an administrator approved a risk lower than the floor with acceptRiskLowering; one event instead of definition_approved, with risk set to the new risk, CC-167), tool_removed (a tool left the registered manifest), kill_switch_set and kill_switch_cleared (an administrator switched a server or a tool off or on again, CC-194; sub is the administrator, the tool is in tool and the system in server; the free text of the administrator is not part of the event) and hidden_characters (an approval of a pending definition was refused because a name or a text in it holds a forbidden character of the text hygiene rule, CC-121, CC-250; outcome denied, sub is the administrator, tool is the tool and definitionHash the hash that was sent; the tool stays pending). A call that needs a fresh MFA and has none is admin_change with reason step_up_required and outcome denied; CC-250 adds the lifting of a kill switch and acceptRiskLowering to those calls. For the broker, service_account_key_set and service_account_key_deleted (an administrator set, replaced or removed the key of the platform's account in a system, CC-251; component broker, outcome ok, sub and username of the administrator, server mcp-<system>, kvVersion of the version written or, for a delete, the one that was current (absent when there was no entry), expiresAt when the key has one; never the value, the username or the password of the account, nor a hash of them). service_account_key_deleted is also written by the delete of a system that had a key (next to system_deleted, same fields). A refused write is admin_change with denied and step_up_required or not_admin, a secret store that does not answer is secret_store_unavailable. For definition_approved the sub is the administrator; for a tool of an adapter the same event carries the risk and the action the administrator gave (CC-193, CC-207), which is how a classification differs from any other approval; for user_purged it is the purged user, and the calling identity (the certificate CN mcp-offboarding) is not a field of this schema. Other reasons are not defined. For event authentication it is the rejection code: for the internal JWT (receiver: server, broker) one of the vectors (missing_token, bad_signature, unknown_kid, alg_not_allowed, wrong_issuer, wrong_audience, expired, replayed_jti, service_token_not_allowed, tool_mismatch, invalid_claims, lifetime_too_long, not_yet_valid, request_id_mismatch, tool_missing, tool_not_allowed, test_key_not_allowed, malformed; for the sidecar of an adapter also classification_missing, a tools/call without mcp_risk and mcp_action, CC-226); for the token of the AI client at the gateway (C1, CC-120): missing_token, malformed, bad_signature, unknown_kid, alg_not_allowed, wrong_issuer, wrong_audience, expired, not_yet_valid, invalid_claims, and for infrastructure failures client_certificate_rejected, jwks_unavailable, replay_store_unavailable (the last two with errorCode upstream_unavailable). The gateway also emits authentication for its own admin port (C5 /admin/v1 and /actuator/prometheus, CC-125): client_certificate_rejected for a client certificate that is missing, not from the internal CA, lacks the clientAuth purpose or has a CN that the operation does not allow, and the token reasons above for a BFF token that fails validation (aud mcp-gateway-admin). replay_store_unavailable is emitted only by receivers of the internal JWT (servers through the starter, the broker), never by the gateway. The broker uses these two names (jwks_unavailable, replay_store_unavailable) in an event authentication with outcome denied like the servers do; key_source_unavailable and jti_store_unavailable are not defined (CC-197). The broker also records the rejection of the token itself (bad_signature, expired, replayed_jti and the other codes of the internal JWT above) as an event authentication with outcome denied and without server, sub or tool, not as the event of the operation it was about to authorize; for a rejected token it writes no credential_resolve or connection_change (CC-211). decision is optional on authentication (deny when present); the broker writes none (CC-212). The gateway may aggregate or sample client_certificate_rejected on its admin port (for example one event per source address per minute, or a counter in its metrics) so that a scanner cannot flood the SIEM (CC-125).

suppressedCount.description: On the summary event of CC-191, written when the window of a user and reason closes: how many refusals of that reason were left out of the audit in that window (CC-190). Only the gateway writes it, on policy_decision or tool_call with decision deny. The summary may carry suppressedTargets as well.

suppressedTargets.description: On the summary event of CC-191, next to suppressedCount (CC-195): how many different targets (tool names, or hashes of filters and cursors, never written to the event) the left out refusals of that window concerned. Lets the SIEM tell one repeated call from a sweep over many tools.

argsLength.description: Length in bytes of the serialized arguments; the only trace of arguments allowed in audit.

definitionHash.description: Hash of the tool definition an admin_change concerns (CC-133): for definition_approved the approved hash, for definition_submitted the hash of each pulled definition that waits (one event per tool), for tool_removed the hash of the removed entry. Together with sub (the administrator) and tool it tells afterwards who approved which definition. Not a secret.

kvVersion.description: On admin_change with reason service_account_key_set or service_account_key_deleted (CC-251): version of the entry in the KV v2 store that was written, or that was current when the entry was removed. Not a secret.

expiresAt.description: On admin_change with reason service_account_key_set (CC-251): the expiry the administrator gave the key; absent for a key without one.

tlsMode.description: On admin_change with reason server_connection_approved or server_connection_changed (CC-249): the trust mode approved or proposed.

fingerprint.description: On admin_change with reason server_connection_approved or server_connection_changed (CC-249): SHA-256 of the DER of the leaf certificate approved or newly seen; absent for plain. Never the certificate.

allOf.description: kvVersion and expiresAt (CC-251) belong to the two admin_change reasons of the service account key and to nothing else; they are metadata of the entry, never part of the key.

The filter field (CC-174, CC-186) belongs to the gateway and to four events only, and a rejected filter has none (nothing valid was normalized): authentication is covered by its closed field list, broker and server events by component.

Authenticator events (CC-094) always say how they ended (outcome) and why (reason). The field list stays closed through additionalProperties: there is no field that could carry a code, a seed or an otpauth URI.

Rejected authentication (CC-071, CC-120): emitted by a receiver of the internal JWT (server, broker) and by the gateway for the token of the AI client (C1). Closed list of fields (propertyNames): everything that comes from the claims of the unverified token (sub, username, client, tool, risk, resource, filter, policyRevision, credentialType) is forbidden, and so is any part of the token. Carries the rejection code in reason.
replay_store_unavailable belongs to receivers of the internal JWT (server, broker); the gateway has no replay store for tokens of the AI client (CC-125).
